newsitem.title: USA: EPA sees final pesticide test rules by summer.
newsitem.headline: EPA sees final pesticide test rules by summer.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said it hoped to issue by early summer final rules that would ease the agency's scientific tests of some low-risk pesticides.
"It will probably be a couple of months before the rules are finalized," Dan Barolo, director of EPA's pesticides program, said in an interview. "We hope to have this done by early summer."

Last year, the agency proposed a new set of controversial regulations that would allow pesticide manufacturers to self-certify that toxicity studies submitted to the EPA to register a pesticide were accurate.
"We want to maximize our resources at the agency and we'd rather have our people review and analyze the more complex studies," he said.
Currently, the EPA must review sometimes more than 100 different hazard and chemical tests before approving a pesticide.
"We then would audit periodically to make sure they are following through as they said, and there are huge penalties if they violate the proposed regulation," Barolo said.
Earlier on Tuesday, a group of 22 environmental and farmworker groups challenged the EPA proposal as unsafe.

"EPA should be moving toward tighter control over safety reviews, not a relaxing of those standards, as proposed," the group, the National Coalition Against the Misuse of Pesticides, said in a statement.
"The question of verifying and reviewing a pesticide's physical/chemical characteristics goes to the heart of the chemical's potential hazard to human health and the environment," the groups said.
